# Title: Diagnosis

## Description
The failing test `FrequencyTest.testPcts()` in the `Frequency` class from the Apache Commons Math library is failing due to a method `getPct(Object v)` using `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)` instead of `getPct(Comparable)`. The method is deprecated and should be replaced by `getPct(Comparable)` according to the bug report.

## Step-by-Step Explanation
1. The failing test `FrequencyTest.testPcts()` adds values to a `Frequency` object `f` and then calls `f.getPct((Object) Integer.valueOf(3))` expecting a result of `0.5`.
2. The bug report highlights that the `getPct(Object v)` method is deprecated and should be replaced by `getPct(Comparable)`.
3. The code snippet from the bug report shows the deprecated implementation of `getPct(Object v)`:
    ```java
    @Deprecated
    public double getPct(Object v) {
        return getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v);
    }
    ```
4. The bug occurs because the `getPct(Object v)` method internally calls `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)` instead of `getPct(Comparable)` as required for non-cumulative percentage calculation.
5. To fix the bug, the usage of `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)` should be replaced with `getPct((Comparable) v)` in the `getPct(Object v)` method.

This diagnosis suggests that the method needs to be fixed by replacing the call to `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)` with `getPct((Comparable) v)` in the `Frequency` class.

## Suggested Methods to Fix
- `org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.getPct(Object)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
